headline: Level at half time.
Four goals in twenty-six minutes.
story.lead: United had 61% of the ball, 72% of the final third, 33 shots to nine and 35 touches in the Ipswich box against 12 in ours — and went in at 1–1. The game turned between the 52nd and 56th minute: a post, a block on the six-yard line, a corner that produced three shots in fifteen seconds, and then a deflected own goal.
story.sub: Shot for shot, Ipswich’s chances were better — 0.19 non-penalty xG a shot on Twelve’s count against United’s 0.16. That is the same imbalance as Hull, where it read 0.20 to 0.10. The difference this time was volume: 32 non-penalty attempts instead of 19. Two matches is not a trend, and every 26/27 figure on this page carries its sample count.
story.shots_h2: 42 shots, and the sharper ones were Ipswich's
story.shots_intro: Each circle is a shot, sized by expected goals. United’s 33 attempts are worth 5.76 — 5.00 across the 32 that were not the penalty, at 0.16 a shot. Bruno’s spot kick carries the other 0.76: Twelve’s total less their own non-penalty figure, not a value we modelled. Ipswich took nine for 1.49, 0.17 a shot; Twelve’s headline 0.19 divides the same 1.49 by eight open-play shots, so the two are not interchangeable. Twelve of United’s were blocked and 11 reached the target, seven of them saved by Scherpen — the plot draws 13 blocks because WhoScored files the six-yard block on 52 minutes as on target while the event stream calls it blocked.
story.sits_note: Eight of United’s 33 shots were set pieces — four from corners, two direct free kicks, a throw-in and the penalty. The corner on 53 minutes produced three of them inside fifteen seconds, and the own goal followed three minutes later.

quadrant.note: Top right is doing both. Ipswich sat deep from the first whistle, so box presence was the scarce resource.
